summary:
During long-duration missions to Mars, astronauts face up to 44-minute round-trip communication delays with Earth, making real-time telemedicine impossible while microgravity silently degrades bone density, cardiovascular health, and vision. To solve this, we developed HELIX (Human Extra-Atmospheric Longitudinal Intelligence & Telemetry eXchange), an offline-first, autonomous astronaut health cockpit.

HELIX replaces clinical alarm fatigue with an interactive 3D Ghost Twin that visually compares in-flight physiological drift against the astronaut’s pre-launch Earth baseline. It integrates live smart-shirt ECG telemetry, Web Audio acoustic biomarkers to screen cognitive fatigue, and edge computer vision to guide SANS optic-nerve ultrasound scans without an onboard doctor.

Instead of reactive sirens, HELIX calculates a Predictive Health Runway™ (days remaining before medical safety boundaries breach) and synthesizes multi-hazard data into “One Thing Today”—a single, prioritized countermeasure per shift.

HELIX is critical because deep-space crews cannot wait 44 minutes for Houston in medical crises. It delivers true clinical autonomy to ensure astronauts return home safely.
details: HELIX is an offline-first, autonomous astronaut health cockpit developed to bridge the critical 44-minute communication delay between Earth and deep-space crews en route to Mars. Built with React 19, TypeScript, Three.js, Web Audio API, FastAPI, and Supabase, HELIX solves the dual threats of silent microgravity degradation and cognitive alarm fatigue by mapping multi-channel telemetry directly onto an interactive 3D Ghost Twin that visually compares in-flight physiological drift against the astronaut’s pre-launch Earth baseline. The system ingests continuous 60 FPS smart-shirt ECG waveforms, extracts cognitive fatigue from 5 seconds of voice via client-side acoustic spectrograms (FFT), and uses edge computer vision to verify probe gel coupling and target lock during autonomous SANS eye ultrasounds. Grounded in NASA Human Research Program standards and NASA-STD-3001 human factors, HELIX replaces screaming ICU alarms with a Predictive Health Runway™ (projecting days remaining before clinical limits breach) and synthesizes all risks into “One Thing Today”—a single prioritized countermeasure with instant equipment-failure backups. By delivering resilient point-of-care medical autonomy without requiring an onboard doctor, HELIX ensures astronaut survival on interplanetary voyages while providing a blueprint for extreme remote healthcare in Antarctica, submarines, and rural clinics on Earth.
